1. Executive Summary & Problem Formulation

Predictive Maintenance (PdM) is essential for aircraft engine safety and airline operational economics. Standard deep learning regressors output a single point estimate for Remaining Useful Life (RUL). However, point estimates ignore model epistemic uncertainty, and standard threshold rules fail when real-world constraints such as spare-part lead times and technician bottlenecks exist.

Core Project Achievement

By connecting a PyTorch LSTM model with Monte Carlo Dropout uncertainty bounds to a 4-Agent Scheduling Layer, this project cuts turbofan fleet costs by 75.05% compared to Run-to-Failure and prevents 96 out of 100 in-service catastrophic breakdowns.

3. Data Cleaning & Sensor Selection

Raw engine telemetry cannot be fed directly into deep learning models due to uninformative features and disparate measurement scales:

  • Dropped Constant Sensors (Variance = 0): Sensors s_1, s_5, s_10, s_16, s_18, s_19 and setting_3 have zero variance in FD001. Flat features create dead weights and dilute gradients without diagnostic utility.
  • Selected 14 Informative Sensors: s_2, s_3, s_4, s_7, s_8, s_9, s_11, s_12, s_13, s_14, s_15, s_17, s_20, s_21 show strong monotonic drift as High-Pressure Compressor (HPC) wear progresses.
  • Min-Max Normalization: Maps all 14 channels into [0, 1] using training set statistics.
  • Piecewise Capped RUL (125 Cycles): Wear during early flight hours is negligible. Capping at 125 cycles stabilizes early predictions and prevents the network from fitting noise in healthy engines.

4. LSTM RUL Model & Comprehensive Working Mechanism

Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks are designed specifically to overcome the Vanishing Gradient Problem of vanilla RNNs, enabling models to learn degradation trends spanning 30+ cycles.

Figure 2: Architectural Anatomy and Mathematical Information Flow inside the LSTM Cell

Internal Gating Equations

An LSTM cell maintains a Cell State ($C_t$) for long-term memory and a Hidden State ($h_t$) for short-term working output:

1. Forget Gate: f_t = σ(W_f · [h_(t-1), x_t] + b_f) (Decides what to discard) 2. Input Gate: i_t = σ(W_i · [h_(t-1), x_t] + b_i) (Decides what to update) 3. Candidate: C~_t = tanh(W_c · [h_(t-1), x_t] + b_c) (Creates candidate updates) 4. Memory Highway: C_t = f_t ⊙ C_(t-1) + i_t ⊙ C~_t (Additive cell state update) 5. Output Gate: o_t = σ(W_o · [h_(t-1), x_t] + b_o) (Decides what to emit) 6. Hidden State: h_t = o_t ⊙ tanh(C_t) (Final operational output)

PyTorch Implementation Architecture

Input (Batch, 30, 14) ──► nn.LSTM(input_size=14, hidden_size=64, batch_first=True) ──► Last Time Step Slice [:, -1, :] (Batch, 64) ──► nn.Dropout(p=0.20) ──► nn.Linear(64, 32) + nn.ReLU() ──► nn.Dropout(p=0.20) ──► nn.Linear(32, 1) ──► Scalar RUL Prediction

5. Predicted RUL & Uncertainty Quantification (Monte Carlo Dropout)

Rather than disabling dropout during test inference, Monte Carlo Dropout (Gal & Ghahramani, 2016) keeps dropout active (p=0.20) across N_MC = 30 stochastic forward passes:

• Predictive Mean: μ_RUL = (1 / N_MC) * Σ y^(s) • Epistemic Uncertainty: σ_RUL = sqrt( (1 / (N_MC - 1)) * Σ (y^(s) - μ_RUL)^2 ) • Conservative 95% Bound: [RUL_lower, RUL_upper] = [max(0, μ - 1.96*σ), μ + 1.96*σ]

Operational Impact: Planning maintenance against RUL_lower provides a safety buffer against overestimation, which is the primary cause of tarmac failures in deterministic scheduling.

7. Viva Voce Defense Guide (Key Technical Q&A)

Q1: Why choose LSTM over vanilla RNNs?

Vanilla RNNs suffer from the vanishing gradient problem due to repeated matrix multiplications during backpropagation through time. LSTMs introduce an additive Cell State highway that allows error gradients to propagate back across 30+ cycles without exponential decay.

Q2: Why drop 7 sensors out of 21?

Sensors s1, s5, s10, s16, s18, s19 and setting_3 have zero variance in subset FD001. Flat features contribute zero diagnostic signal and create dead weights in neural networks.

Q3: Why cap the RUL target at 125 cycles?

Wear in early cycles is negligible. An uncapped linear target forces the network to fit random sensor noise during healthy operation. Capping at 125 focuses representational capacity on the non-linear degradation regime.

Q4: Why plan with RUL_lower instead of the mean?

A point estimate of 20 cycles with standard deviation of 6 has a high probability of failing before 10 cycles. Planning with RUL_lower hedges against overestimation risk, eliminating 96% of catastrophic failures.
